thread.title: 10 things to know about the Arizona job market, wages, Trump tax cuts and your paycheck

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: 10 things to know about the Arizona job market, wages, Trump tax cuts and your paycheck
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 18, 2018, 2:39pm MST Arizona ended 2017 with an uptick in unemployment and slightly lower job gains than usual for the month of December but healthy gains in private sector wages. That comes after the U.S. Department of Labor reported weekly jobless claims nationally came in at 220,000 last week. That’s the lowest in 45 years, since 1973. It also comes the same week the Dow Jones Industrial Average passed 26,000 for the first time and companies continue to give bonuses or raises after the tax cuts signed into law by President Donald Trump . Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) said yesterday it was giving $2,500 in stock options to its employees and would hire 20,000 in the U.S. as part of a $350 billion domestic investment and $250 billion in repatriation of money kept in offshore tax havens. That all comes after Trump and Congress passed tax cuts slicing corporate rates from 35 percent to 21 percent and are granting U.S. companies such as Apple to bring back money kept offshore at a one-time 15 percent rate. Apple said it will pay $38 billion in taxes on that offshore money into the U.S. Here are other takeaways from the latest batch of job, wage and economic numbers: 1. Fatter paychecks Private sector wages in Arizona rose by 6.2 percent in 2017, according to state economists. That compares to 2.6 percent nationally. Arizona wages went way down during the recession and last real estate crash but are now outpacing the U.S. 2. Who to thank Some of that has to do with increased minimum wage last year after voters approved a measure hiking the baseline pay rate to $10 per hour from $8.05. Arizona’s minimum wage is $10.50 this year. 3. Banks, insurance and business service boost wages But some sectors that tend toward higher wages also saw pay boosted last year. Business services saw hourly wages go up 6.5 percent ($27.56 per hour versus $25.18 per hour) and finance and insurance jobs were up 4.4 percent up to $29.01 per hour in 2017 from $27.78 in 2016. And those numbers don’t include bonuses and wages workers are getting this year after the Trump. Banks such as Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) and Phoenix-based Western Alliance Bancorp (NYSE: WAL) have given bonuses or raise to workers. 4. Restaurants and bars still hiring Restaurants and bars — which minimum wage critics argued would get hit hard by increased wage — hired 12,700 new workers last year statewide. That’s most of any sector. Retail has lost jobs in Arizona and nationally but wages could be helped with Wal-Mart Stores Inc. (NYSE: WMT) bumping up its starting pay to $11 per hour and giving tax-related raises. 5. More workers Arizona’s labor force gained 79,647 workers last year a 2.45 percent gain. The state posted 1.6 percent population growth last year. That’s the same as 2016 but up from previous, post-recession years. 6. Four out of 10 not working or looking for a job But the state’s labor participation rate isn’t going up. Arizona’s labor participation rate — which counts employed workers and those seeking jobs — is 60.6 percent. That compares to 62.7 percent nationally. That Arizona number means almost 40 percent of working-age adults in the state are on the economic and workplace sidelines. 7. Unemployment edges up Arizona’s unemployment rate ended the year at 4.5 percent. That was up from 4.3 percent in November and more than 4.1 percent U.S. jobless rate, according to the Arizona Office of Economic Opportunity. Arizona’s unemployment rate at the end of 2016 was 5 percent. 8. Jobs in Phoenix The unemployment rate is in the Phoenix metro area closed out 2017 at 3.9 percent. It was 3.7 percent in November and 4.1 percent a year ago. The Phoenix metro area added 36,800 private sector jobs in 2017. That is 90 percent of Arizona’s job gains last year. 9. Arizona job gains Arizona added 40,900 private sector jobs for all of 2017. That is a 1.7 percent gain. For December, the state added 9,500 private sector jobs. That is below the recent average of businesses hiring 10,600 employees during December, according to the state Office of Economic Opportunity. 10. Manufacturing Manufacturers — a big focus of Trump — added 2,900 jobs statewide in December and 5,600 jobs for the year. That is up from 1,400 jobs gains in 2016. But the semiconductor industry shed 800 jobs last year. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 18, 2018, 2:39pm MST
